findings.title: Photos can download twice during Save all
findings.description: `tap()` keeps a fixed `ready` list across download gaps without rechecking whether `save(p)` has handed over an item. If someone taps an individual photo during that gap, its download starts and is marked handed over, but the batch downloads the same photo again.

location.code_snippet:
+        if (i) await wait(DOWNLOAD_GAP);
+        try { download(ready[i].file); handed.add(ready[i].pid); } catch (e) { console.warn('download failed', ready[i].file?.name, e); }

evidence.explanation: The per-photo path updates the same handed set independently, while Save all snapshots its batch before waiting and does not inspect that set again inside the loop.

findings.title: A verifying photo disappears from counts
findings.description: `saveBatch()` counts an unfinished photo only while its key remains in `incoming`, but the chunk handler deletes that key before `done()` verifies the hash and adds the file to `files`. A Save all tap during verification sees the photo as neither ready nor still arriving and can say there is nothing new to save.

location.code_snippet: +  for (const fid of incoming.keys()) if (!fid.startsWith('thumb:') && !files.has(fid)) arriving++;

evidence.explanation: The chunk handler removes the incoming key before calling the asynchronous verifier; the verified file is added only after hashing, leaving a period when neither map contains the photo.

findings.title: Narrow phones lose the details control
findings.description: The new Save all button makes the right-anchored, non-wrapping `#bar` wider without changing its layout. On a narrow phone, the leftmost Keep details checkbox falls off-screen, and the page's hidden horizontal overflow prevents scrolling to it.

findings.title: Blocked downloads get marked as saved
findings.description: `createSaveAll` marks each photo as handed over right after `download(ready[i].file)` starts, without waiting for the browser to confirm the save, and it shows the `Saved N` toast before the download loop runs. A download the browser silently blocks or cancels, or one that throws (which is only sent to `console.warn`), is skipped by every later Save all tap and never retried, so the user is told N files were saved when some never were.

location.code_snippet: +        try { download(ready[i].file); handed.add(ready[i].pid); } catch (e) { console.warn('download failed', ready[i].file?.name, e); }

citations.citation: Record completion only after the work succeeds

evidence.explanation: The checklist requires completion state to be set only after the operation confirms success, but here `handed.add(ready[i].pid)` runs immediately after a fire-and-forget `download(ready[i].file)`, and the single-photo path in `save()` does the same with `downloadFile(file); saveAll.handed.add(p.pid)`. The share path, by contrast, waits for the share promise before marking files. The toast is emitted before the loop, and the loop's failure branch only logs, so the user sees a success message. The test at line 177 of tests/saveall.test.mjs confirms that a throwing download is silently skipped and retried later, but no test or UI message covers what the user actually sees.

findings.title: Two TESTING.md rows share the F13 ID
findings.description: The new TESTING.md row reuses requirement ID `F13` with test levels `Unit, System`, while the existing row for F13 is `Acceptance`. The table is keyed by requirement ID, so the results for F13 are ambiguous to a reader.

location.code_snippet: +| F13 | Unit, System | `tests/saveall.test.mjs`: 12 received photos go to the share sheet in one call, made inside the tap. Own photos, thumbnails and prints never fetched are left out and full photos still arriving are counted. A batch the share sheet can't take, or no share sheet, downloads one at a time `DOWNLOAD_GAP` apart. A cancel does nothing. Another failure downloads nothing until the next tap, which downloads everything not yet handed over, then the share sheet is tried again. Nothing is handed over twice, and a tap during a download batch starts nothing. The two-browser test taps Save all on a laptop: all 5 received files download byte-identical, and a second tap downloads nothing (exists) |
